name: Jafri Email Inspector – Diagnostics & Troubleshooting
author: Tanveer Jafri

sections.description:
SMTP plugins help you configure email sending. Jafri Email Inspector helps you understand why it’s failing.

Contact form emails not arriving? WooCommerce order emails missing? Password reset emails nowhere to be found? Jafri Email Inspector gives you a plain-English diagnosis instead of a wall of technical logs.

What Jafri Email Inspector checks

  • Whether WordPress’s mail system is working
  • SMTP/mail provider connection problems, authentication failures, timeouts
  • SPF, DKIM, and DMARC DNS records for your domain
  • Recent email send failures, with the likely cause
  • WooCommerce email configuration (only when WooCommerce is active)
  • Hosting and setup traps: disabled PHP mail(), plugins that replace or intercept wp_mail(), an admin email with no MX records, disabled WP-Cron, and high failure rates in your log
  • One click “Copy report for support” so you can share a clean diagnostic summary

What Jafri Email Inspector is not

Jafri Email Inspector is not an SMTP configuration plugin. It is designed to work alongside WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP, Post SMTP, Easy WP SMTP, and hosting-provided mail systems — detecting and explaining their behavior rather than replacing them.

Honesty about “delivered”

Jafri Email Inspector never tells you an email was “delivered” just because WordPress handed it off successfully. It clearly distinguishes “WordPress accepted the email for sending” from actual inbox delivery, which generally requires provider-side confirmation that this plugin cannot access on its own.

Privacy

Jafri Email Inspector stores a lightweight local log of outgoing email attempts (recipient, subject, source, status, and technical error details when available) to help diagnose problems. SMTP passwords, API keys, and authentication tokens are never logged. Full email content is not stored unless you explicitly enable that option. Logs are automatically pruned to a configurable retention limit. Uninstalling the plugin does not delete your data unless you have explicitly enabled that option in Settings.

Known Limitations

  • DKIM detection relies on a list of commonly used selectors and cannot discover custom/uncommon selectors automatically.
  • Jafri Email Inspector can confirm that WordPress handed a message to its configured mail transport; it generally cannot confirm actual inbox delivery without a provider-specific integration.
  • Source attribution (which plugin generated an email) is a best-effort heuristic and is always labeled with a confidence level.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the jafri-email-inspector folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Jafri Email Inspector in your admin menu and click “Run Full Email Check”.
sections.faq:
Does this replace my SMTP plugin?

No. Jafri Email Inspector is a diagnostic tool. It detects and works alongside SMTP plugins such as WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP, Post SMTP, and Easy WP SMTP.

Does Jafri Email Inspector send my mail through its own servers?

No. All checks and test emails run through your own site’s existing mail configuration.

Will Jafri Email Inspector fix my SPF/DKIM/DMARC records for me?

No. Jafri Email Inspector never modifies DNS automatically and never invents a record. It explains what it found and points you toward your provider’s documentation.

Is my email content stored?

By default, no — only metadata needed for diagnosis (recipient, subject, status, error). You can optionally enable storing full email content in Settings, with a clear privacy warning.

I used to have “Email Doctor” installed — will I lose my settings or logs?

No. Jafri Email Inspector is the renamed continuation of the same plugin. Updating in place keeps your existing settings, email logs, and database intact — nothing is reset by the rename.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New diagnostics: disabled PHP mail(), wp_mail() replaced by another plugin, something intercepting mail via pre_wp_mail, admin email domain without MX records, high failure rate, disabled WP-Cron, and a clear “nothing logged yet” hint for new installs.
  • New: summary chips (problems, warnings, notes, passed) above the findings.
  • New: “Copy report for support” button on the dashboard.
  • Fix: after an update the dashboard no longer shows a stale cached check, so new diagnostics appear immediately.
  • Fix: support email link used the old plugin name in its subject line.
  • Fix: “Leave a Review” now links straight to the WordPress.org review form.
  • Readme: shorter description and screenshot captions.

1.1.0

  • Renamed the plugin to “Jafri Email Inspector – Diagnostics & Troubleshooting” (previously distributed as “Email Doctor”; new slug: jafri-email-inspector). Existing settings, email logs, and scheduled cleanup are fully preserved for anyone upgrading.
  • Translations now load automatically, per current WordPress.org convention for hosted plugins.
  • Security hardening around AJAX request handling and database queries.

1.0.1

  • Fix: outgoing-mail logging now hooks wp_mail_succeeded instead of a mistimed wp_mail filter callback, so success/failure, transport, and sender are captured accurately for every email instead of sometimes producing duplicate or incomplete log rows.
  • Fix: the dashboard’s automatic Health Check no longer re-runs DNS lookups on every page view; results are cached briefly and the “Run Full Email Check” button always forces a fresh check.
  • Fix: when more than one SMTP/mail plugin is detected, the plugin now reports “multiple mail-related plugins detected” instead of silently picking one.
  • Hardening: stored email content (only saved when explicitly enabled) now renders in a sandboxed iframe in the Email Logs detail view as defense-in-depth, in addition to existing server-side sanitization.

1.0.0

  • Initial release (as “Email Doctor”): Email Health dashboard, Test Email, Email Logs, Diagnostics engine, DNS & Authentication checks (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), WooCommerce email health and safe test sends.

short_description: Find out why WordPress emails fail: plain-English diagnosis of SMTP, SPF, DKIM, DMARC and sending errors. Works alongside your SMTP plugin.
